newsitem.title: USA: Latin Bradies sluggish, Russian paper slumps.
newsitem.headline: Latin Bradies sluggish, Russian paper slumps.

text.p: Latin American Brady bonds were sluggish on Thursday ahead of Friday's U.S. payrolls report, while Russian debt issues slumped on news President Boris Yeltsin would undergo heart surgery, traders said.
"The most important news happened in Russia with Yeltsin's health. In the Latin locales nothing happened," said one Brady bond trader at a U.S. investment bank.
Word of Yeltsin's health rocked the prices of Russian Vnesh loans and MinFins, even though most analysts said the revelations merely confirmed what most players already suspected.
Dollar-denominated Vnesh dropped more than two points during early trade, but recovered to close down 1-5/8 for a bid price of 61.
"There was some buying at the end of the London day, but not enough to bring it back," said Ingrid Iversen, debt strategist at UBS Securities.
Iversen said the market could expect continued volatility, if only because player use the Yeltsin issue to take profits.
"One of the main thing to note is that people were sitting on significant profits," Iversen said. "I don't think that investors have changed their view of Russia."
As of September 4, Russian paper on the JP Morgan Emerging Markets composite index had risen 77 percent year-to-date.
Across Latin America, Brady bonds slipped with U.S. Treasuries amid uncertainty over U.S. interest rates and a dearth of news from the region.
"The market was slightly down on the day," said Tulio Vera, managing director at Bear Stearns. "Everybody is pretty much sitting tight waiting for the number tomorrow morning."
Argentine FRBs slipped 1/4 to 78-3/4, while Brazilian Cs lost 1/2 to 64-1/8. The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond fell 20/32 to yield 7.15 percent.
"Everything followed the T-bond today, but it was very quiet," one Brady trader said. "There was not much volume."
